requirement:
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later. For citation assessments, additional node reads and selected excerpts are recorded as SDK dependencies under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs` states no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. It has test edges and no implementation edges, and the review roots are empty. I checked each clause for an implementation choice it prescribes.

- **"The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies."** This names what ends up in the evidence. It doesn't name a type, library, signature or interface. A harness could collect the inputs in a hook, a wrapper around the tools, or a post-hoc log replay. The recorded evidence would be the same, so the choice is discretionary.
- **"Using the evidence input formats defined by `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`, `requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and `requirements.definitions.inputs`."** This constrains the serialized output, not how the code is organized. Those formats are specified and checked in their own requirements, which this text only cites.
- **"The harness MUST create these records itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later."** This says the harness, not the model, produces the records, so validation can check them. That is observable: the records are present and validate, and the model cannot forge or omit them. It doesn't prescribe a particular delegation or named interface. Any harness-side mechanism that produces valid records meets it.
- **The citation-assessment sentence.** Additional node reads and selected excerpts must be recorded as SDK dependencies under `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` and `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. This is an observable recording outcome. The detailed rules (fingerprint at delivery, tag reselection, empty `used`) belong to those cited requirements. They are judged there, not here.

Every clause describes observable recording behavior, so the test edges are the right evidence and no implementation marker is needed.

behavioral: I found no adequacy gap. The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. I did not request any implementation source.

**Mandatory inputs recorded.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` checks that the evidence inputs include the `fn[ready_test]` and `fn[ready]` outline inputs and a `terms.readiness` definition input.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` checks the three input forms across several determinations. It finds a requirements input for the subject, a definition input and an outline input. It also checks that outline inputs hold exactly `file`, `item` and `hash`.

**Additional reads recorded.**
- The ollama test reads `extra.txt` twice and asserts that the recorded inputs equal `outline_inputs_for_lines(...)`. Delivery is therefore recorded once, by selector and hash only.
- The same test asserts that a failed read of `absent.txt` records nothing.
- The same test asserts that the plain search and `list_sources` record nothing.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[optional_requirement_and_example_reads_preserve_the_complete_declarations]` reads a requirement and an example. It asserts that the record contains exactly the requirements-input format: `requirements`, `matches`, and `text` as full raw lines. It then edits the book and asserts that validation reports a stale input naming the subject and `requirements.illustration`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[behavioral_review_discovers_implementation_locations_without_receiving_their_bodies]` shows that a location-only edge lookup records nothing. Reading the target later records `fn[ready]` exactly once.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` checks recorded inputs and delivery through the Bedrock backend.

**Selected search dependencies.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[relying_on_a_helper_excerpt_makes_edits_to_that_helper_stale]` selects a search excerpt through `finish_search`. It asserts that the selected helper `fn[assert_refusal]` and the explicitly read `fn[read_me]` are recorded. It asserts that the unselected `fn[unselected]` is not recorded.
- The same test edits the helper between the search and the finish. It asserts that validation then reports the helper as changed.
- `src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` checks the details. Empty `used` adds nothing. A selection records the node and fingerprint from the original snapshot, even after the file changes. Repeated selection and invalid calls leave the recorded inputs unchanged.

**Harness creates the records so evidence validation can check them.** The CLI tests run `habeas::validate_repository` on the harness-produced evidence. The ollama test, the helper test and the optional-read test do this. Together they assert both acceptance and staleness findings.

**Citation and example assessments, and SDK dependencies.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_and_example_assessments_record_selected_and_explicit_reads]` covers both subject kinds. A selected search excerpt (`fn[first]`), an explicit read (`fn[second]`) and an optional definition read (`terms.unused`) are all recorded. The definition input has the exact text lines. Untouched `fn[untouched]` is not recorded.
- `src/agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]` covers recording on delivery only. It checks the node and edge dependencies, and that a failed provider response records nothing.

text: :::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records

itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later. For citation assessments, additional node reads and selected excerpts are recorded as SDK dependencies under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs

Habeas MUST store the source dependencies selected by `finish_search` under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.inputs` as outline inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`. Each input identifies the file, selector, and structural hash from the snapshot that supplied the selected excerpt.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. For display and reference coverage, it MUST derive the inclusive line range
from the first and last bytes of the SDK outline item's attachment-inclusive
span under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.item_span`. An empty
span covers the line at its start. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{req} inputs

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs
For each selected tag, the harness records the node identity and fingerprint
from the snapshot that produced the delivered excerpt. If the excerpt also shows source owned by other outline nodes, record those nodes’ read fingerprints as well. Selecting a tag again
preserves the original dependency. Earlier selections survive later calls.
An empty `used` list adds no dependency. Unselected excerpts and the match set
add none either. An invalid call leaves all recorded inputs intact.
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
